correctness.rationale: For primitive frequency differences, expansion modulo p² reduces Fourier sums to at most two stationary terms; odd-order phases cannot cancel. Imprimitive sums reduce to prime-level permutations, whose mixed cubic-linear obstruction is proved using a quadratic character sum. This yields saturated p-point residue fibres, only (p+1)/2 allowable reduced slopes, and (by the independently inspected published Rédei–Megyesi theorem) an affine reduced line. Every lift choice is then checked for pairwise orthogonality, and unique counting follows. Exact cyclotomic arithmetic checker passed 46,228 Fourier-zero cases and 826,668 reduced graph functions; experiments alone are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification and exact count of all exponential Fourier bases for a canonical nonlinear polynomial graph over every prime-square ring (p≥5), resolving infinitely many discrete spectral-design instances. The arithmetic p mod 3 dichotomy changes independent local fibre orientations and therefore the count by an exponential-in-p factor. Unlike a routine check of spectral existence or a single numerical invariant, it describes every maximizing orthogonal frequency configuration with a uniquely decodable parametrization. No downstream theorem is claimed.
